label: bug
title: fix(payments): validate durable refund intents before provider side effects
problem: Online refunds call the provider before validating sale-state, line membership/remaining quantity and restock eligibility. Using unchanged reverse/applyReversal source methods with mocked I/O, a partial refund naming a UUID-shaped line absent from the sale produced: provider refund accepted → database transaction → 422 REFUND_LINE_NOT_FOUND; no reversal inserted. This is a control-flow reproduction, not a live money or PostgreSQL test. Provider success followed by local failure can leave an unrecorded external refund.
scope: Validate and durably reserve a refund intent, bound to normalized request/hash and refundable limits, before provider I/O. Use a stable provider key and recover/reconcile ambiguous outcomes.
criteria: Invalid sale state, line, quantity and restock requests make zero provider refund calls.
Persist an auditable intent before provider effects; record success, failure and unknown outcomes.
Same-key replay cannot refund twice; a changed payload with the same key is rejected.
Concurrent distinct-key requests cannot exceed remaining money, line or restock limits.
Provider success followed by database failure/process restart recovers to exactly one consistent reversal.
Add regressions for all above, including real PostgreSQL concurrency; preserve cash/manual reversal behaviour.
boundaries: Do not hold a database transaction open across network I/O as the sole fix. Do not claim real-provider verification from mocked tests.
body:
## Problem and evidence
Online refunds call the provider before validating sale-state, line membership/remaining quantity and restock eligibility. Using unchanged reverse/applyReversal source methods with mocked I/O, a partial refund naming a UUID-shaped line absent from the sale produced: provider refund accepted → database transaction → 422 REFUND_LINE_NOT_FOUND; no reversal inserted. This is a control-flow reproduction, not a live money or PostgreSQL test. Provider success followed by local failure can leave an unrecorded external refund.

Audit date: 2026-11-15. Baseline revision: `d4b3ac178ef7fd03078caca70fafd32843abeaca`.
Related: #17, #21, #22.

- [apps/api/src/sales/sales.service.ts#L1589](https://github.com/arkinara/modern-pos/blob/d4b3ac178ef7fd03078caca70fafd32843abeaca/apps/api/src/sales/sales.service.ts#L1589)
- [apps/api/src/sales/sales.service.ts#L1764](https://github.com/arkinara/modern-pos/blob/d4b3ac178ef7fd03078caca70fafd32843abeaca/apps/api/src/sales/sales.service.ts#L1764)
- [apps/api/src/payments/payments.service.ts#L605](https://github.com/arkinara/modern-pos/blob/d4b3ac178ef7fd03078caca70fafd32843abeaca/apps/api/src/payments/payments.service.ts#L605)

## Scope
Validate and durably reserve a refund intent, bound to normalized request/hash and refundable limits, before provider I/O. Use a stable provider key and recover/reconcile ambiguous outcomes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Invalid sale state, line, quantity and restock requests make zero provider refund calls.
- [ ] Persist an auditable intent before provider effects; record success, failure and unknown outcomes.
- [ ] Same-key replay cannot refund twice; a changed payload with the same key is rejected.
- [ ] Concurrent distinct-key requests cannot exceed remaining money, line or restock limits.
- [ ] Provider success followed by database failure/process restart recovers to exactly one consistent reversal.
- [ ] Add regressions for all above, including real PostgreSQL concurrency; preserve cash/manual reversal behaviour.

## Boundaries
Do not hold a database transaction open across network I/O as the sole fix. Do not claim real-provider verification from mocked tests.

## Planning
Priority: P1. Source: Project 19 repository audit (2026-11-15).

label: bug
title: fix(printing): connect kitchen station queues to Android delivery
problem: Station routing persists jobs and exposes state/retry endpoints, but no station-job API consumer or kitchen-ticket renderer was found in mobile application source. PrintQueueService processes sale receipts, not station queues. No server worker connects those jobs to printer transport either. API job records and a loopback receipt test do not complete a kitchen delivery flow. This is a source-traced integration gap, separate from physical hardware verification.
scope: Connect order creation/amendment/cancellation to durable station events and implement Android station claiming, rendering, printer selection and delivery state handling.

AMEND and CANCEL tickets retain the same stable order reference and correct item changes.

Automated app-to-two-fake-transports tests cover routing, amendment, cancellation, disconnect and restart; document the physical acceptance recipe.
boundaries: Keep cashier/physical execution on Android. Do not move checkout into the web app or claim hardware acceptance from fake transports.
body:
## Problem and evidence

PrintQueueService processes sale receipts, not station queues. No server worker connects those jobs to printer transport either. API job records and a loopback receipt test do not complete a kitchen delivery flow. This is a source-traced integration gap, separate from physical hardware verification.

- [ ] AMEND and CANCEL tickets retain the same stable order reference and correct item changes.

## Boundaries

label: bug
title: fix(mobile): support bounded offline session recovery and refresh retries
problem: AuthController.build restores sessions only through online refresh; any Dio network failure returns null, and ModernPosApp then shows SignInScreen. An outage plus app restart blocks cashier and queue UI even though encrypted queued records survive. No persisted authorized offline profile/catalog was found. Timed refresh also schedules another timer only on success, so a transient non-401 refresh failure loses automatic retries. These findings are source-traced, not physical Android reproductions.
scope: Define the supported offline session lifetime and revocation/reconnect policy, then implement bounded authorized offline restart, scoped catalog/settings snapshots and resilient refresh retries.
criteria: A previously authorized session within the documented offline allowance can restart without network and access its scoped cashier/queue UI.
Persist scoped catalog/settings needed for offline capture; display snapshot age and offline limitations.
Expired/missing offline authorization requires sign-in; a new unauthenticated install cannot sell offline.
Transient refresh failure schedules bounded retries/reconnect recovery; 401/revocation follows the explicit policy.
Sign-out or account/outlet changes do not expose another user's/outlet's cached data or replay its queue without authorization.
Tests cover restart while offline, expired authorization, transient refresh outage/reconnect and durable queue preservation.
boundaries: Do not bypass authentication unconditionally or promise server acceptance/stock reservation while offline. If product policy excludes restart-capable sales, record the explicit decision and narrow UI/docs instead of reporting full offline acceptance.
body:
## Problem and evidence
AuthController.build restores sessions only through online refresh; any Dio network failure returns null, and ModernPosApp then shows SignInScreen. An outage plus app restart blocks cashier and queue UI even though encrypted queued records survive. No persisted authorized offline profile/catalog was found. Timed refresh also schedules another timer only on success, so a transient non-401 refresh failure loses automatic retries. These findings are source-traced, not physical Android reproductions.

Audit date: 2026-11-15. Baseline revision: `d4b3ac178ef7fd03078caca70fafd32843abeaca`.
Related: #4, #12, #19.

- [apps/mobile/lib/features/auth/auth_controller.dart#L36](https://github.com/arkinara/modern-pos/blob/d4b3ac178ef7fd03078caca70fafd32843abeaca/apps/mobile/lib/features/auth/auth_controller.dart#L36)
- [apps/mobile/lib/features/auth/auth_controller.dart#L118](https://github.com/arkinara/modern-pos/blob/d4b3ac178ef7fd03078caca70fafd32843abeaca/apps/mobile/lib/features/auth/auth_controller.dart#L118)
- [apps/mobile/lib/app.dart#L32](https://github.com/arkinara/modern-pos/blob/d4b3ac178ef7fd03078caca70fafd32843abeaca/apps/mobile/lib/app.dart#L32)

## Scope
Define the supported offline session lifetime and revocation/reconnect policy, then implement bounded authorized offline restart, scoped catalog/settings snapshots and resilient refresh retries.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A previously authorized session within the documented offline allowance can restart without network and access its scoped cashier/queue UI.
- [ ] Persist scoped catalog/settings needed for offline capture; display snapshot age and offline limitations.
- [ ] Expired/missing offline authorization requires sign-in; a new unauthenticated install cannot sell offline.
- [ ] Transient refresh failure schedules bounded retries/reconnect recovery; 401/revocation follows the explicit policy.
- [ ] Sign-out or account/outlet changes do not expose another user's/outlet's cached data or replay its queue without authorization.
- [ ] Tests cover restart while offline, expired authorization, transient refresh outage/reconnect and durable queue preservation.

## Boundaries
Do not bypass authentication unconditionally or promise server acceptance/stock reservation while offline. If product policy excludes restart-capable sales, record the explicit decision and narrow UI/docs instead of reporting full offline acceptance.

## Planning
Priority: P1. Source: Project 19 repository audit (2026-11-15).

label: bug

criteria: Production startup rejects missing/placeholder secrets, unsafe cookie settings and missing/invalid explicit allowed origins.
Production has explicit payment-provider/mode configuration; implicit mock fallback is rejected.
Sandbox provider routes return unavailable in production even if MOCK is mistakenly selected.
Local/test sandbox use requires explicit documented opt-in; normal local development remains reproducible.
Automated startup/controller checks cover safe and unsafe combinations; diagnostics do not reveal secrets.
Update environment/deployment docs and retain session, CSRF and outlet authorization checks.
boundaries: Do not claim a deployed vulnerability was observed. Do not add real provider credentials or change financial calculations.

## Scope
Select one exact Android device/version and printer model/firmware/transport for the initial supported configuration and execute the physical acceptance checklist.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Record device, Android version, printer model/firmware, transport, code page, width and supported commands.
- [ ] Verify permission denial/regrant, pairing/connect, test output, receipt totals/layout/encoding and reconnection on real hardware.
- [ ] Observe physical kitchen ORIGINAL/AMEND/CANCEL tickets with stable references after the station integration fix.
- [ ] Exercise mid-write disconnect/process restart; UNKNOWN never silently resends and COPY is visibly marked.
- [ ] Exercise app restart/offline recovery and checkout reconnect; reconcile one sale/payment and exact stock effects.
- [ ] Attach dated logs and paper/photo evidence; mark only the tested combination supported and leave other combinations pending.

## Boundaries
Requires access to selected hardware. Mock channels, APK builds and TCP listeners cannot substitute for paper evidence; do not claim all transports verified.

title: ops: validate deployment recovery, off-host backups and operational ownership
problem: The existing staging dry run does not establish production operations. Logical restore documentation is useful historical evidence, not a current recovery objective.

Configure health/error monitoring and actionable alerts; exercise a controlled failure and record the notification/recovery.
Verify least-privilege access and redacted logs, and enforce production config checks.

Attach dated environment/version, restore timing and integrity evidence; leave unresolved infrastructure requirements open.
boundaries: Do not deploy to production, move production data or change external infrastructure without the applicable authorization. This ticket prepares and verifies a reviewable release configuration.

## Problem and evidence
The existing staging dry run does not establish production operations. Known limitations include absent automated off-host backup/retention, monitoring/alerting and production TLS/secret management. Logical restore documentation is useful historical evidence, not a current recovery objective.

- [ ] Attach dated environment/version, restore timing and integrity evidence; leave unresolved infrastructure requirements open.

## Problem and evidence
All original project items were Done while acknowledged external acceptance remained pending. A final closing gate must follow the integrity fixes and explicit device/provider/operator/operations acceptance rather than treating historical green CI as complete operational proof.

Audit date: 2026-11-15. Baseline revision: `d4b3ac178ef7fd03078caca70fafd32843abeaca`.

## Scope
Run final acceptance on one pinned release candidate only after the linked prerequisites are closed with evidence. Track any explicit scope exclusions and preserve them in the owner handoff.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every dependency has passing evidence or an explicit documented release-scope decision; no silent waiver of required hardware/payment support.
- [ ] Pin candidate commit, environment, schema/toolchain versions and supported device/printer/provider configuration.
- [ ] CI, PostgreSQL integration, browser and physical/provider acceptance results match the candidate or include a justified delta rerun.
- [ ] End-to-end sale/payment/stock/report/receipt reconciliation and refund recovery pass across retry, restart and disconnect scenarios.
- [ ] Deployment/restore runbooks, limitations and operational ownership are current and reviewable.
- [ ] Record final acceptance decision and unresolved risks; production go-live remains a separate explicit authorization.

## Boundaries
Do not close this gate merely because implementation or CI passes. Do not expand features here; reopen/link actionable failures to prerequisite tickets.
